politeJa: そこまでじゃないです
english: it's not that bad; not that much
use: Toning down what someone said, whether it was too gloomy or too glowing.

example.romaji: taihen? iya, soko made ja nai yo.
example.ja: 大変？いや、そこまでじゃないよ。
example.english: Rough? Nah, it's not that bad.

examplePolite.romaji: taihen desu ka? iie, soko made ja nai desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 大変ですか？いいえ、そこまでじゃないですよ。
examplePolite.english: Is it hard? No, it's not that bad.

notes: Close to sou demo nai, but it disputes how much, not whether.

use: Agreeing that a remark is spot on, often something you hadn't put into words yourself.

example.romaji: ieteru. ano hito, itsumo okureru yo ne.
example.ja: 言えてる。あの人、いつも遅れるよね。
example.english: You said it. That guy's always late.

notes: Politely, say tashika ni or sou desu ne instead.

use: Granting that something someone mentions is part of the reason.

example.romaji: a, sore wa aru kamo. saikin nete nai shi.
example.ja: あ、それはあるかも。最近寝てないし。
example.english: Oh, that could be it. I haven't been sleeping.

examplePolite.romaji: a, sore wa arimasu ne. saikin nete inai node.
examplePolite.ja: あ、それはありますね。最近寝ていないので。
examplePolite.english: Oh, that's a factor. I haven't been sleeping lately.

notes: Sore mo aru adds one more reason: 'that's part of it too'.

use: Said when someone points out something you hadn't noticed but now see is true.

example.romaji: iwarete mireba, saikin kare minai ne.
example.ja: 言われてみれば、最近彼見ないね。
example.english: Now that you mention it, I haven't seen him lately.

examplePolite.romaji: iwarete mireba, saikin kare o mimasen ne.
examplePolite.ja: 言われてみれば、最近彼を見ませんね。
examplePolite.english: Now that you mention it, I haven't seen him recently.

notes: Often followed by tashika ni, 'that's true'.

use: Changing your mind a little when someone gives a good counterpoint.

example.romaji: sore mo sou da ne. ja, ashita ni shiyou.
example.ja: それもそうだね。じゃ、明日にしよう。
example.english: Fair point. Let's do it tomorrow then.

examplePolite.romaji: sore mo sou desu ne. ja, ashita ni shimashou.
examplePolite.ja: それもそうですね。じゃ、明日にしましょう。
examplePolite.english: That's true. Let's make it tomorrow, then.

notes: Sore wa sou da kedo is the opposite move: granting the point, then pushing back.

use: Granting someone's point before giving your own view.

example.romaji: sore wa sou da kedo, ima wa okane nai yo.
example.ja: それはそうだけど、今はお金ないよ。
example.english: That's true, but I don't have the money right now.

examplePolite.romaji: sore wa sou desu kedo, ima wa okane ga nai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: それはそうですけど、今はお金がないんです。
examplePolite.english: That's true, but I don't have the money at the moment.

notes: Often trails off after kedo, letting the tone carry the 'but'.

use: Pushing back on a general claim without flatly calling it wrong.

example.romaji: takai kara oishii? sou to mo kagiranai yo.
example.ja: 高いからおいしい？そうとも限らないよ。
example.english: Pricey means tasty? Not necessarily.

examplePolite.romaji: takai kara oishii desu ka? sou to mo kagirimasen yo.
examplePolite.ja: 高いからおいしいですか？そうとも限りませんよ。

notes: The wider pattern X to wa kagiranai means 'X isn't always so'.

politeJa: 気持ちはわかりますけど
english: I get how you feel, but...
use: Showing sympathy before disagreeing or giving advice.

example.romaji: kimochi wa wakaru kedo, ima yameru no wa mottainai yo.
example.ja: 気持ちはわかるけど、今辞めるのはもったいないよ。
example.english: I get how you feel, but quitting now would be a waste.

examplePolite.romaji: kimochi wa wakarimasu kedo, ima yameru no wa mottainai desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 気持ちはわかりますけど、今辞めるのはもったいないですよ。
examplePolite.english: I understand how you feel, but it'd be a shame to quit now.

notes: The wa matters: you understand the feeling, not that you agree with the plan.

use: Disagreeing with someone's opinion, clearly but without attacking it.

example.romaji: uun, watashi wa sou wa omowanai kana.
example.ja: うーん、私はそうは思わないかな。
example.english: Hmm, I don't really think so.

examplePolite.romaji: watashi wa sou wa omoimasen kedo.
examplePolite.ja: 私はそうは思いませんけど。
examplePolite.english: I don't see it that way, myself.

notes: Adding kana or kedo softens it a lot; said bare, it can sound blunt.

kana: それはちがうとおもう
politeJa: それは違うと思います
use: Saying a fact or opinion is wrong; to omou keeps it from sounding like a flat correction.

example.romaji: iya, sore wa chigau to omou. kare wa warukunai yo.
example.ja: いや、それは違うと思う。彼は悪くないよ。
example.english: No, I don't think that's right. It's not his fault.

examplePolite.romaji: iie, sore wa chigau to omoimasu. kare wa warukunai desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: いいえ、それは違うと思います。彼は悪くないですよ。
examplePolite.english: No, I don't think that's right. He's not to blame.

notes: Chigau also means 'different'; here it means 'wrong'.

polite: doushite sou omou n desu ka?
politeJa: どうしてそう思うんですか？
use: Asking for someone's reasons, out of curiosity or to challenge them.

example.romaji: e, nande sou omou no? setsumei shite.
example.ja: え、なんでそう思うの？説明して。
example.english: Huh, why do you think so? Explain.

examplePolite.romaji: doushite sou omou n desu ka? oshiete kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: どうしてそう思うんですか？教えてください。
examplePolite.english: Why do you think so? Please tell me.

notes: Doushite is softer than nande, so use it when politeness matters.

use: Said in frustration when someone repeats your point as their own or hasn't been listening.

example.romaji: dakara, sou itteru jan! kiite nakatta no?
example.ja: だから、そう言ってるじゃん！聞いてなかったの？
example.english: That's what I'm saying! Weren't you listening?

notes: Jan is a casual 'isn't it'; here it sounds pushy, so keep it for friends.

use: Playfully calling out an obvious fib or brag among close friends.

example.romaji: kyou wa nomanai? uso tsuke.
example.ja: 今日は飲まない？嘘つけ。
example.english: You're not drinking today? Yeah, right.

notes: It's a command form, so it can sound harsh to people you don't know well. Uso tsuki is the noun 'liar'.

use: Said when someone guesses right; also heard at prize draws and on winning tickets.

example.romaji: sou, atari! yoku wakatta ne.
example.ja: そう、当たり！よくわかったね。
example.english: Yep, you got it! How did you guess?

examplePolite.romaji: hai, atari desu. yoku wakarimashita ne.
examplePolite.ja: はい、当たりです。よくわかりましたね。

notes: The opposite is hazure: 'wrong guess' or 'a dud'.

use: Casual, slightly teasing praise when a friend does better than expected.

example.romaji: zenbu seikai? yaru jan!
example.ja: 全部正解？やるじゃん！
example.english: All correct? Nice going!

notes: It implies surprise, so don't say it to a superior; politely, say sugoi desu ne.

use: Comforting someone right after a small slip, especially in sports or games.

example.romaji: donmai! tsugi wa ganbarou yo.
example.ja: ドンマイ！次は頑張ろうよ。
example.english: Don't worry about it! We'll get it next time.

notes: From English 'don't mind', but only used this way; for bigger worries say ki ni shinaide.

use: A friendly remark when you notice a new haircut, usually followed by a compliment.

example.romaji: are, kami kitta? niau ne!
example.ja: あれ、髪切った？似合うね！
example.english: Oh, did you get a haircut? It suits you!

examplePolite.romaji: are, kami kirimashita ka? niaimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: あれ、髪切りましたか？似合いますね。
examplePolite.english: Oh, did you get your hair cut? It looks good.

notes: Kiru covers a salon cut too; there's no separate 'have it cut' form.

politeJa: 雰囲気変わりましたね
english: you look different; you seem different
use: Said when someone's look or vibe has changed since you last met.

example.romaji: hisashiburi! nanka fun'iki kawatta ne.
example.ja: 久しぶり！なんか雰囲気変わったね。
example.english: Long time no see! You look different somehow.

examplePolite.ja: お久しぶりです。雰囲気変わりましたね。
examplePolite.english: It's been a while. You look different.

notes: Usually meant kindly; add ii ne to make it a clear compliment.

src: なんかいいことあった？
ja: なんかいいことあった？
kana: なんかいいことあった？
politeJa: 何かいいことありましたか？
use: Said when someone looks happier than usual, smiling or humming.

example.romaji: nikoniko shite, nanka ii koto atta?
example.ja: ニコニコして、なんかいいことあった？
example.english: You're all smiles. Did something good happen?

examplePolite.romaji: ureshisou desu ne. nanika ii koto arimashita ka?
examplePolite.ja: 嬉しそうですね。何かいいことありましたか？
examplePolite.english: You look happy. Did something good happen?

notes: Nanka is the casual nanika ('something'); it's also the filler 'like'.

use: Introduces what really happened or what you really want, against what was said or assumed.

example.romaji: honto wa, ikitakunakatta n da.
example.ja: ほんとは、行きたくなかったんだ。
example.english: Actually, I didn't want to go.

examplePolite.ja: 本当は、行きたくなかったんです。
examplePolite.english: To be honest, I didn't want to go.

notes: Hontou wa is the full form, used in careful speech.
